proposals.before: Hanzhi marched on Jin and Jiang. Quanyi struck and seized Heyang. Hanzhi ran to Li Keyong; Jin sent help and penned Quanyi tight.
proposals.after: Hanzhi marched on Jinzhou and Jiangzhou. Quanyi struck and seized Heyang. Hanzhi fled to Jin; Jin sent help and penned Quanyi tight.
proposals.reason: 攻晉、絳 names the prefectures Jin and Jiang, not the Jin state; 罕之奔晉 then names that state. Rendering both as Jin and inserting Li Keyong collapses the two 晉 and adds a personal name the Chinese does not use here.

proposals.before: Tang ended; he served Liang and asked for a new name. The Founder called him Zongyi.
proposals.after: Tang ended; he served Liang and asked for a new name. The Founder called him Zongshi.
proposals.reason: 太祖賜名宗奭 is Zōngshì (奭), not Zongyi (義). The same error is repeated when Lady Chu addresses him in s0027.

proposals.before: Defeated at Gaoxian, Zhu Wen sickened on the march home. He summered at Quanyi’s Festival Garden ten days and forced Quanyi’s wife and daughters.
proposals.after: Defeated at Tiaoxian, Zhu Wen sickened on the march home. He summered at Quanyi’s Festival Garden ten days and forced Quanyi’s wife and daughters.
proposals.reason: 蓚縣 is Tiao/Xiu county (also written 蓨縣), not Gaoxian. Gao does not match the character.

proposals.before: His wife Lady Chu was quick and had a tongue like a blade. She went straight in and snapped: “Zongyi? A dirt farmer, nothing more!
proposals.after: His wife Lady Chu was quick and had a tongue like a blade. She went straight in and snapped: “Zongshi? A dirt farmer, nothing more!
proposals.reason: Quoted 宗奭 is the same Liang-bestowed name as s0020; Zongyi misreads 奭 as 義.

proposals.before: Zhu Youqian, styled Deguang, came from Xuzhou.
proposals.after: Zhu Youqian, styled Deguang, came from Xu Prefecture.
proposals.reason: 許州 is Xu Prefecture (modern Xuchang), not 徐州. The idiomatic Xuzhou collapses two different prefectures.

proposals.before: Li Keyong came out of Ze and Lu, met Huaiying at Jie, broke him utterly, chased to Baijing Ridge, burned torches into him at night, broke him again, and Liang pulled off.
proposals.after: The Prince of Jin came out of Ze and Lu, met Huaiying at Jie, broke him utterly, chased to Baijing Ridge, burned torches into him at night, broke him again, and Liang pulled off.
proposals.reason: Chinese has 晉王. The campaign follows 太祖遇弒 in 912; Li Keyong had already died in 908, so the personal name is a mistranslation of the Jin princely title.

proposals.before: Youqian slept drunk in Li Keyong’s tent. The Prince looked him over and told his men: “All that honor—and such short arms!”
proposals.after: Youqian slept drunk in the Prince of Jin’s tent. The Prince looked him over and told his men: “All that honor—and such short arms!”
proposals.reason: Continues the 晉王 of s0069. Li Keyong is not in the Chinese and cannot be this 晉王 after 908.

proposals.before: Edict: Jiji kill Lingde at Suizhou; Wang Sitong kill Lingxi at Xuzhou; Xia Luqi wipe out the clan at Hezhong.
proposals.after: Edict: Jiji kill Lingde at Suizhou; Wang Sitong kill Lingxi at Xu Prefecture; Xia Luqi wipe out the clan at Hezhong.
proposals.reason: 許州 is Xu Prefecture (Xuchang), not 徐州. The idiomatic Xuzhou repeats the same prefecture collapse as elsewhere in the chapter.

proposals.before: Lu Siduo came from Linhuang in Cao.
proposals.after: Lu Siduo came from Linhuang in Chan Prefecture.
proposals.reason: Chinese 澶州臨黃 is Linhuang in Chan Prefecture (Chanzhou), not Cao (曹州).

decisions.after: Hanzhi marched against Jin and Jiang Prefectures. Quanyi struck behind him and seized Heyang. Hanzhi fled to Jin, whose troops came to his aid and pressed Quanyi hard in siege.
decisions.reason: The first 晉 and 絳 are Jin and Jiang Prefectures, while 罕之奔晉 refers to the Jin polity. The revision distinguishes them and removes Li Keyong, whom this sentence does not name.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 罕之出兵攻晉、絳……罕之奔晉，晉遣兵助罕之

decisions.reason: 宗奭 is pronounced Zongshi. Zongyi misreads 奭 as 義 and conflicts with the extraction's correctly romanized Chinese name.

decisions.after: After his army was defeated at Tiao County, Zhu Wen fell ill on the road back to Luoyang. He spent ten days escaping the summer heat at Quanyi's Festival Garden, where he forced Quanyi's wife and daughters to submit to him.
decisions.reason: The place is 蓨縣, conventionally Tiao County, not Gaoxian. The revision also completes the English sense of 皆迫淫之 instead of leaving 'forced' without stating what the women were forced to do.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 太祖兵敗蓨縣，道病，還洛

decisions.reason: Lady Chu addresses Zhang Quanyi by the Liang-bestowed name 宗奭, which is Zongshi, not Zongyi.
許州 is Xu Prefecture, centered on modern Xuchang, and is distinct from Xuzhou 徐州. The replacement corrects the mistaken place name.

decisions.after: The Prince of Jin came from Ze and Lu to rescue him. He met Huaiying at Jie County and routed him, pursued him to Baijing Ridge, and attacked by torchlight at night. Huaiying was defeated again, and the Liang army withdrew.
decisions.reason: The Chinese names the Prince of Jin, not Li Keyong, who had died in 908. The parallel Jiu Wudai Shi account says Youqian appealed to Zhuangzong for this rescue; the revision also replaces the unidiomatic phrase 'burned torches into him.'

sourceWitness.excerpt: 晉王出澤、潞以救之……夜秉炬擊之

decisions.after: Youqian fell asleep drunk in the Prince of Jin's tent. The prince looked him over and said to his attendants, 'The Prince of Ji may be very exalted, but unfortunately his arms are short!'
decisions.reason: This is the same Prince of Jin as in s0069, not Li Keyong. The revision restores the full force of the quoted assessment rather than compressing it into an unexplained fragment.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 友謙醉寢晉王帳中……冀王雖甚貴，然恨其臂短耳

decisions.after: An edict ordered Jiji, Prince of Wei, to kill Lingde at Suizhou, Wang Sitong to kill Lingxi at Xu Prefecture, and Xia Luqi to exterminate the rest of the family at Hezhong.
decisions.reason: 許州 is Xu Prefecture rather than Xuzhou 徐州. The revision also restores Jiji's title and turns the telegraphic proposal into grammatical English while preserving all three commands.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 詔魏王繼岌殺令德於遂州，王思同殺令錫於許州

decisions.after: Lu Siduo was from Linhuang in Chan Prefecture.
decisions.reason: 澶州 is Chan Prefecture, not Cao Prefecture 曹州. The revision restores both the correct administrative name and natural biographical English.

claimRetractions.reason: s0012 names the Jin polity, not Li Keyong personally, so this explicit personal-name claim was created solely from the mistranslation and must be removed.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 罕之奔晉，晉遣兵助罕之

claimRetractions.reason: The repaired sentence does not mention Li Keyong, so it cannot explicitly attest his role as a warlord in this unit.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 罕之奔晉，晉遣兵助罕之

claimRetractions.reason: Fleeing to Jin attests Li Hanzhi and the Jin polity, not Li Keyong as an explicitly mentioned person, so this personal attestation must be removed.
